The main takeaway from our work is that

the anti-association factor and the eukaryotic initiation factors 1, 2, and 5 are all present in the postribosome supernatant of the liver extract and are not in any of the salt wash ribosomal protein fractions.

the anti-association activity in the postribosmal supernatant of mammalian liver extracts is contained in a 25,500 Mr protein that is distinct from the 60 S subunit binding activity in the salt-washed ribosomes.

the eukaryotic initiation factors 1, 3, and 4B are sufficient to reconstitute the binding of eIF2-GTP-Met-tRNA(i)(M) ternary complexes to 48 S preinitiation complexes, and that the binding of ternary complexes is not affected by eIF5.
